finding: 2026-09-25 Drew ruling + PR #2427 review correction: retires the LOSING duplicate at each destination targeted by more than one source row for the SAME player (472 collision groups measured, 35 of them pure name-superset/diacritic pairs, spanning 65 retired entries). Exactly one mover per destination lands via a move-* file; every other same-player row at that destination is retired here, AFTER its mover has landed -- the lane's retire predicate needs the twin to exist at the canonical address before deleting the loser is safe.
rulings: OWNER RULING (Drew, 2026-09-25 ~21:20Z): the unnumbered 2026 Topps baseball Super Box parallel carries ONE spelling, "Silver Crackle Foil". Five non-canonical spellings of the same unnumbered non-auto rung were measured under setKeys topps/topps-series-1/topps-series-2/topps-update/topps-chrome: "Silver Crackle Foil (Super Box exclusive)" (1,712), "Silver Crackleboard Foil Board"/"Crackleboard Foil" (350+150=500), "Silver Crackle Foilboard" (375), bare "Silver Crackle" (0 found). Colour rungs are DISTINCT cards and excluded by construction.

REVISED 2026-09-25 after PR #2427 review (REQUEST CHANGES). The original retire list was INVERTED: it called catalog-explode-actuals-2026-08-12 occupants 'checklist-grade' by a hand-rolled source-prefix regex that never matched `^catalog-explode`, so it accepted derived rows as checklist-grade and would have retired 109 real checklist-transcribed rows in favour of derived duplicates. Every grade decision below is now made with the REAL catalogAuthorityOf (backend/dist/services/catalog/catalogAuthority.service.js), never a source-prefix guess. catalogAuthorityOf classifies catalog-explode-actuals-2026-08-12 and ingest-auto-seed as DERIVED (matches the DERIVED regex's `catalog-explode`/`ingest-auto-seed` stems) and checklistinsider-*/checklistcenter-*/baseballcardpedia-ladders-* as CHECKLIST.

DESTINATION COLLISIONS ARE DEDUPED. 472 of the 1,738 destinations this fold touches are targeted by 2-3 source rows (1,276 of 2,587 in-scope rows), because the same card is transcribed under multiple non-canonical spellings by multiple checklist packages (baseballcardpedia-ladders, checklistcenter, checklistinsider all mint their own copy). Exactly ONE mover is kept per destination -- the fullest player name agreeing with the checklist majority, tie-broken checklistinsider > checklistcenter > baseballcardpedia -- and the remaining same-player duplicates are RETIRED, never moved, after the mover lands (see retire-after-move.json). 65 of the retire-after-move entries (spanning 35 of the 472 groups) are pure name-superset pairs ("Bobby Witt" vs "Bobby Witt Jr.", diacritic pairs like "Julio Rodriguez"/"Julio Rodríguez", or a trailing checklist-position tag like " CL"); the fuller name is kept as the mover in every one.

CROSS-PLAYER COLLISIONS ARE PARKED, NOT RESOLVED HERE. Where two DIFFERENT players' names land on the same canonical destination (a genuine numbering disagreement between sources, not a spelling variant), this lane parks nothing and moves nothing automatically -- every such row is reported to Drew in the PR body for a ruling, and appears in NO list file.

DESTINATION COMPUTED BY THE REAL computeHobbyIqCardId, NEVER STRING-HACKED. Every destination id was produced by the built dist/services/portfolioiq/hobbyIqCardId.service.js, changing ONLY parallel to "Silver Crackle Foil" -- one axis.

APPLY ORDER: LAST. Every entry's `evidence` names the mover it must follow; entries flagged `afterDerivedRetire:true` additionally depend on retire-derived-occupants.json + move-03 having landed first. Sequence: retire-derived-occupants -> move-01/move-02 (independent) -> move-03-after-derived-retire -> THIS FILE.

MOVER SELECTION RULE: fullest player name (by token-superset containment) agreeing with the checklist majority, tie-broken checklistinsider > checklistcenter > baseballcardpedia(-ladders). Losing rows are LISTED HERE, never silently dropped.
